item.title: Bill Belichick’s Malachi Toney assessment may worry UNC fans before Miami game
item.description: Miami brings the No. 1 ranking to Kenan Stadium on Saturday night, the first time the nation’s top-ranked team has played in Chapel Hill since 2019, and North Carolina coach Bill Belichick opened the week by breaking down the player at the center of the Hurricanes’ offense. What he said on Monday about defending sophomore receiver Malachi Toney sounded like a warning to his own secondary. Toney has 66 catches for 952 yards and 11 touchdowns through seven games. His last two outings produced 27 receptions. He caught 11 passes for 154 yards and two scores in the double-overtime win over Florida State, then had 16 catches for 194 yards and three touchdowns against Pittsburgh on Saturday, breaking the Miami single-game receptions record he had set earlier this season. Nov 29, 2025; Raleigh, North Carolina, USA; North Carolina Tar Heels head coach Bill Belichick addresses the media after the second half of the game against NC State Wolfpack at Carter-Finley Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jaylynn Nash-Imagn Images Belichick was asked at his Monday press conference about double-teaming Toney. “He finds ways to get open even when he is double-covered. That doesn’t really stop him,” Belichick said . “You would think it would, but not really. He’s made several big plays off double coverage because he knows how to beat double coverage. At his age, that’s pretty impressive. I don’t see any weak points in his game,” he added. Belichick’s defenses built their reputation on taking away what an opponent does best, and double coverage is the most direct way to do that against one dominant receiver. Hearing him concede in public that the tool does not solve Toney is unusual candor from a coach known for giving away almost nothing at a podium. The rest of his scouting report went well beyond getting open. “He’s good at everything. He’s even a good blocker,” Belichick said. “He’s tough. A lot of guys that play that position don’t have that. He’s obviously very explosive, quick, and fast. Good with the ball in his hands … He’s a good returner. He can turn a short play into a long touchdown, like he’s done a bunch of times,” he continued. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Can UNC repeat what it did to Darian Mensah last season? North Carolina held Darian Mensah to a season-low 175 passing yards last season, when he was Duke’s quarterback, though the Blue Devils still won 32-25 in Chapel Hill. Mensah now runs Miami’s offense, and he leads Power Four quarterbacks in touchdown passes. That game is the closest thing Belichick has to a blueprint for Saturday, and the piece that has changed is the receiver he just said a double-team does not stop. item.title: Bill Simmons calls out ‘dumbest’ WNBA leadership decision amid Finals arena fiasco
item.description: Photo by Ali Gradischer/Getty Images Bill Simmons is not thrilled whatsoever about Game 6 of the WNBA Finals being played at 12:30 p.m. ET. The sports analyst was quite harsh in his response to the news. Despite concerns that the WNBA Finals might need to be played in a venue seating just 3,500 fans in Atlanta, Games 3 and 4 were played at State Farm Arena in front of huge crowds. Game 6, which is set to be played in Atlanta on October 29, was facing some scheduling conflicts that have resulted in an interesting solution. The WNBA released a statement explaining that the game will now tip off at 12:30 p.m. ET, with the Atlanta Hawks moving their game to later at night in the same arena. A Finals game starting at noon and earlier than that for a huge chunk of the country is far from ideal, and it’s getting quite a bit of backlash. Bill Simmons calls out WNBA leadership’s decision-making all season long after Game 6 statement The series between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries is incredibly tight. Game 6 could see the Valks lift their first-ever championship trophy in just their second season in existence. To have a game that crucial in the afternoon is a bit underwhelming. WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert will be stepping down at the end of this year. This season has been quite a challenge for her and the league hierarchy. Hilariously, after this latest announcement, Bill Simmons has suggested that they have gotten absolutely nothing right. “Incredible! A heroic finishing touch to one of the dumbest leadership seasons in professional sports history. They’ve had like 12 major decisions in 2026 and somehow went 0 for 12. People want to like this league!” Simmons wrote in an X post. Despite all the criticisms, the league has managed to grow once again, and the Finals are a resounding success. Considering that the Valkyries have no arena issues, fans will be hoping that it goes to a Game 7 and the Finals get the incredible ending they deserve. item.title: Can Auburn bounce back again? Alex Golesh points to season’s pattern
item.description: Alex Golesh opened Ole Miss week at his Monday press conference by describing a conversation he had with his Auburn players that morning. It came after a 38-17 home loss to No. 18 LSU that dropped Auburn to 4-3 and 2-3 in the SEC, the first lopsided defeat of Golesh’s first season on the Plains. Byrum Brown completed 15 of 24 passes for 160 yards and was sacked six times , and Golesh did not dress up what he saw on film. “We lacked detail as a whole on Saturday,” Golesh said. “The margins are so tight. You don’t have to play perfect, but you’ve got to play really sound,” he added . “We’ve had the ability to reset as this year’s gone. We’ve had to lick our wounds, come back and play good football … If we don’t, it’ll be a really long week. If we do, we’ve got an opportunity to go on the road and beat a really good football team,” Golesh said. item.title: Why Spencer Danielson keeps turning down Power Four interest at Boise State
item.description: Baylor fired Dave Aranda on Sunday after a loss to Kansas, and Spencer Danielson’s name turned up among the early candidates for the job. On Monday, at his weekly press conference in Boise, the Boise State coach was asked about the Power Four openings piling up around the sport, and he walked through his answer at length. Boise State is 6-1, 3-0 in the Pac-12 and ranked No. 20, and Danielson is 30-9 with three Mountain West titles and a 2024 College Football Playoff berth since taking over the program, a resume that keeps putting him on Power Four lists. Dec 2, 2023; Las Vegas, NV, USA; Boise State Broncos head coach Spencer Danielson celebrates with running back Ashton Jeanty (2) after 44-20 victory over the UNLV Rebels in the Mountain West Championship at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports “I don’t even let myself go there,” Danielson said of the openings. Asked about a recent inquiry, he said he had “zero interest about anything outside of coaching this team now and in the future,” then explained why in terms he has used throughout his time in Boise. “I absolutely feel like God has called me here. That’s not mythological. These players, this community, what God’s doing here, I’m all chips on the table here,” Danielson said. He also described how those conversations reach him. His agent has told him at times that a school wanted him, and Danielson’s response has stayed the same. “That’s not where I want to go, I feel called here. So we’ve been through it enough that he knows my heart,” he said . Has Danielson turned down this kind of interest before? He gave nearly the same answer a year ago, when 11 FBS programs were searching for coaches. “Absolutely schools have been reaching out. I want to be here, I feel called here,” Danielson said in October 2025. Danielson then signed an extension through the 2030 season in April, a deal that includes a $3.5 million buyout if he leaves before Feb. 28, 2027. That deal added a year to the five-year contract he signed after the 2024 playoff run, which averaged $2.2 million per season. Dec 16, 2023; Inglewood, CA, USA; Boise State Broncos head coach Spencer Danielson reacts during the third quarter against the UCLA Bruins in the Starco Brands LA Bowl at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Hanashiro-USA TODAY Sports “At Boise State, it’s everything. Winning conference championships and College Football Playoff games is why every single player on our team came here,” Danielson told On3 this summer. He did leave himself one opening, and he stated it plainly. “If there’s ever a situation in the future that is intriguing to me, I’ll talk to him,” Danielson said of his agent. That condition covers some future cycle. For this one, with Boise State chasing a second playoff trip and Texas State visiting on Saturday, he described a much smaller world built around the 113 players on his roster. item.title: Report: Mariners set to host Joe Espada, Jason Kanzler to fill empty managerial spot
item.description: Houston Astros manager Joe Espada looks to the field before a baseball game against the Athletics, Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026, in West Sacramento, Calif. (AP Photo/Sara Nevis) Sara Nevis A month after former Mariners manager Dan Wilson announced his decision to step away from the team, the team might be closing in on two potential finalists for his job. MLB.com reports that former Astros manager Joe Espada and the Cubs’ current director of player development Jason Kanzler will be visiting T-Mobile Park for in-person interviews this week, according to several of their sources. Espada went 256-229 during his time as the Astros’ manager and served as the Astros’ bench coach for six years. The Mariners received permission to interview Espada earlier this month . Kanzler, on the other hand, is a dark horse candidate. Kanzler has never managed a team, but the former Minnesota Twins draftee has helped the Cubs develop their farm system for three seasons. MLB.com notes that the Mariners are particularly interested in Kanzler, due to his hitting background, ability to develop players, and his communication skills. This is the third round of interviews for both candidates, and the two will spend time meeting several members of the organization during their respective interviews, according to MLB.com. As for other candidates in the running, MLB.com says Rocco Baldelli, Walker McKinven, Brandon Hyde, Torey Lovullo, and Stephen Vogt’s names all came up at some point, according to their sources. Baldelli was also invited to an in-person interview, but withdrew his name, according to a report from The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal .

item.title: Steve Sarkisian’s grim injury outlook gets brighter for one Texas starter
item.description: Steve Sarkisian offered a bleak injury outlook Saturday night after Texas beat Ole Miss 34-27, a win the Longhorns finished without two starters who went down during the game. By Monday, the news on those two players had split in opposite directions. “Obviously, neither of them look very good,” Sarkisian said after the game. “We essentially played the entire game without Trevor Goosby, and the majority of the game without Cam Coleman,” Sarkisian added. Steve Sarkisian’s Texas Faces Reality Check from Analyst After Top-5 Hype Entering 2026 (Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images) Goosby, the senior left tackle who was carted off in the first quarter while pass blocking, will miss the rest of the season with a knee injury, confirming the worst of Sarkisian’s postgame concern. Coleman, by contrast, practiced on Monday without a green non-contact jersey and appeared to be fine, Chip Brown of 247Sports reported. I’m told #Texas #Longhorns’ WR Cam Coleman, who left the Ole Miss game holding his shoulder after landing awkwardly, practiced Monday without a green jersey and appeared to be fine. https://t.co/mVeYRRIsj9 https://t.co/Up2GzDBN71 — Chip Brown (@ChipBrown247) October 26, 2026 Where Coleman’s injury leaves the Texas passing game Coleman went down on the first play of the third quarter, landing on his left shoulder while diving for a downfield throw from Arch Manning. It was shut out in the third quarter as Ole Miss scored twice to pull within a touchdown, and the Longhorns needed a fourth-quarter rally, sparked by Raleek Brown’s 47-yard run and Manning’s 1-yard touchdown, to retake the lead. Coleman’s absence was one of several factors in that stretch, alongside a strip-sack Ole Miss recovered in the end zone and a reshuffled offensive line playing without Goosby. Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian watches from the sideline during the first half of the Cotton Bowl Classic College Football Playoff semifinal game against the Ohio State Buckeyes at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas on Jan. 10, 2025. Practicing without the non-contact jersey on Monday is an early-week sign, and Texas has not announced a status for Saturday’s game against Mississippi State. The offensive line has no such sign to lean on. Goosby started 22 games over the past three seasons and earned first-team All-SEC honors from the league’s coaches in 2025, and Texas will spend the rest of the season replacing him on Manning’s blind side. “Hopefully we can get these guys back sooner rather than later,” Sarkisian said on Saturday, before the Goosby diagnosis came back. item.title: Steve Sarkisian pushes back on Ole Miss fake punt narrative after Texas win
item.description: Texas held on to beat No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27 on Saturday, and the unit that nearly let the game get away followed Steve Sarkisian into his Monday press conference in Austin. He was asked about the persistent problems on Jeff Banks’ special teams, and his answer put the blame in one specific place. The play that drew the most attention came in the second quarter with Texas up 24-3. Ole Miss punter Oscar Bird, an Australian who kicks rugby-style, took the snap on fourth down, saw open grass and ran for 17 yards to keep the drive going. “Really, wasn’t a fake punt. It was a normal punt with a rugby punter that we didn’t set the edge. And so he’s like, ‘Well, let me just keep running,'” Sarkisian said. Nov 30, 2024; College Station, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian speaks with quarterback Arch Manning (16) during warm ups against the Texas A&M Aggies at Kyle Field. Mandatory Credit: Maria Lysaker-Imagn Images The player responsible for that edge agreed with him. Sophomore defensive end Lance Jackson took the blame after the game and said he never heard the sideline warning that Bird could run. Sarkisian had already called it human error after the game, noting a punter run was always an option for Ole Miss. Sarkisian was just as firm about the other special-teams moment that kept Ole Miss alive. item.title: University of Utah responds after Pat McAfee says he hopes never to return
item.description: College GameDay made its seventh visit to the University of Utah on Saturday, and the No. 10 Utes followed it by beating No. 14 Houston 21-13 to move to 7-0. Two days later, Pat McAfee opened “The Pat McAfee Show” by saying he hopes never to go back, and the university answered him before Monday was over. The trigger was a video posted to the school’s official Instagram account shortly before the broadcast. It featured students poking fun at McAfee, with one calling him “corny” and another “creepy,” and the post has since been deleted. McAfee said students mocking him on their own accounts was fine with him. His problem was that the university put the video out through its own channel right before he went on air to promote the school. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect “It’s the university putting this out,” McAfee said. “I’ve never been more uncomfortable, honestly, in my life,” he said of walking out in front of the crowd. He also framed the discomfort as a safety issue, alluding to the September 2025 killing of conservative activist Charlie Kirk at a Utah Valley University event in Orem, about 40 miles south of Salt Lake City. “Has anything like really scary happened at like a college gathering in the state of Utah recently? Like, do we think we should be amplifying reasons for why people hate my guts as a university?” McAfee said . How did Utah respond to McAfee? “Our goal during the visit was to create lighthearted engagement regarding Pat being back on campus, but we missed the mark,” the university said in a statement to the Deseret News . The statement said university staff review and post everything on official accounts and that the school takes “full accountability for that decision,” which concedes the line McAfee drew between the students and the institution. It added that officials had contacted McAfee directly to express “appreciation and regret.” “We sincerely apologize for creating any perception that Pat was unsafe or unwelcome on our campus,” the university said . “We support Pat and recognize the very real and valid concerns he has around safety and security,” ESPN said in a statement to The Athletic. Utah’s statement also said McAfee and the GameDay crew “are always welcome at the University of Utah.” McAfee had already offered his plan for the next invitation on Monday’s show, joking that he might come down with COVID-19 if GameDay returns to Salt Lake City. Kansas State has won both meetings since Colorado returned to the Big 12, beating Colorado 31-28 at Folsom Field in 2024 before winning 24-14 in Manhattan last November . The Buffaloes recorded their largest series win on Nov. 17, 1990, defeating the Wildcats 64-3 in Boulder. item.title: Bills haven't lost after a bye since Josh Allen was a teenager. Now it's Joe Brady's turn
item.description: Josh Allen was 18 years old the last time the Buffalo Bills lost a game coming off their bye week. Sean McDermott never lost one. Now it's Joe Brady's turn to keep the streak alive. Buffalo has won 11 consecutive games following its bye week, a streak that spans three head coaches and dates to 2015. Sean McDermott went 9-0 following bye weeks during his nine seasons as Bills coach, the most wins without a loss by any head coach in NFL history. Allen has never lost following a bye. Brady will get his first chance to extend the streak when the Bills (5-1) host the Baltimore Ravens (4-3) at 1 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 1, at Highmark Stadium. The Bills have done more than simply win coming off a week of rest. Six of their last seven post-bye victories have come by double digits, with an average margin of victory of 14.9 points. That includes a 35-10 win over the San Francisco 49ers in 2024 and a 40-9 rout of the Carolina Panthers last season. Buffalo's last loss following a bye came Nov. 9, 2014, when the Kansas City Chiefs rallied from a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Bills 17-13. Doug Marrone was Buffalo's coach, Kyle Orton was its starting quarterback and Josh Allen was still in high school. Rex Ryan won both of his post-bye games as Bills coach in 2015 and 2016 before McDermott took over in 2017. McDermott continued the streak throughout his tenure. Brady, who replaced McDermott as head coach in January, inherited a team that has been effective with extra time to prepare. The Bills entered their Week 7 bye riding a two-game winning streak. Buffalo beat the Los Angeles Rams 37-34 in overtime and followed with a 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The break gave Brady and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard an opportunity to evaluate a defense allowing 28.5 points per game. Buffalo has had time to recover from injuries before facing Baltimore, which has lost two consecutive games. The Ravens are coming off a 35-13 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, who scored 35 unanswered points in the second half Sunday. Baltimore played without quarterback Lamar Jackson for the third straight game because of an ankle injury. Coincidentally, the Bengals were coming off their own bye week. item.title: Jorge Martin hopeful of racing in Malaysia after "not complete" fracture diagnosis
item.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin is expecting the arrival of his trusted physiotherapist Aitor Tomas in Malaysia, who has designed the recovery plan that is hoped will enable the Aprilia rider to arrive in the best possible condition for MotoGP's Malaysian Grand Prix. Dr Angel Charte, MotoGP's medical director, will also do everything possible to ensure Martin can take to the track for FP1 at Sepang on Friday morning. The final medical report on Martin's injury indicates a "radial fracture, volar and dorsal". With the bone not displaced and therefore the fracture "not complete", the Spaniard will not require surgery. But there is an unexpected detail that makes optimism more difficult; an old ulnar fracture has resulted in "post-traumatic inflammation" that could complicate the recovery. Although various diagnoses and forecasts have been put forward regarding the rider's options and condition, the only person who knows the full situation is Dr Charte, who has not commented on the matter so far. He will decide whether the rider can ultimately take to the track. Jorge Martín, Aprilia Racing Team Jorge Martín, Aprilia Racing Team Martin suffered a heavy crash in the Australian GP sprint, tumbling through the gravel in the run-off area at Turn 8 having been fighting title rival Marc Marquez for victory. After undergoing a CT scan and various tests in Melbourne, returning to Spain was ruled out, and the rider flew to Malaysia on Sunday night, where a local physiotherapist - with whom he had worked in the past - was waiting for him. Tomas, the physiotherapist hired by Martin's agency and other riders, will arrive in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday and focus on improving the injury as much as possible before the weekend. "I am receiving the treatment I need to recover from the injury and arrive at Sepang in the best possible shape," said Martin in the team's statement ahead of the grand prix. However, he does not want to rush things when it comes to his chances: "It is impossible to make predictions. We have to assess the situation day by day." After the complicated Australian weekend, with Saturday's crash and Sunday's race being abandoned, Martin has only conceded 12 points to Marquez, who now leads the championship by 10 points. Although there are still four grands prix to go (if Qatar goes ahead) and 148 points available, it is clear to everyone that this injury complicates Martin's chances of regaining the championship lead, especially with Marquez having returned to his best form following the shoulder surgery he had to undergo last May. Mandatory Credit: M… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jim Smith Jannik Sinner has not played a competitive tennis match since winning Wimbledon in July, and there is now a very real possibility that his recovery could prove more complicated than initially anticipated. The Italian announced earlier this month that he would miss the remainder of the 2026 season because of persistent inflammation in his right knee. That means no Paris Masters and no ATP Finals and no opportunity to defend his title in Turin. That’s all pretty secondary, though, as the more interesting question concerns 2027. Marco Panichi, Sinner’s former fitness trainer who also spent more than six years working with Novak Djokovic, has offered a potentially concerning assessment of the injury. Speaking to Ubitennis , Panichi discussed the possibility that Sinner is dealing with iliotibial band syndrome, commonly known as ITBS. His warning was relatively simple. If that is indeed the problem, Sinner could remain sidelined for a considerable period. So what exactly is ITBS, how long does recovery take and what might it mean for one of the world’s best tennis players? Why might Jannik Sinner struggle with ITBS? The iliotibial band is a thick strip of connective tissue that runs along the outside of the thigh, connecting structures around the hip to the upper tibia. It essentially helps stabilize the hip and knee during movement. The famed ITBS develops when repeated loading creates irritation and pain around the outer knee, particularly where the band passes over the lower portion of the femur. It is commonly associated with distance running, but tennis players are also vulnerable because of the repeated acceleration, braking and changes of direction their sport demands. That last part is relevant to Sinner. His game depends heavily on exceptional lateral movement, rapid recovery between shots, and the ability to maintain balance while striking aggressive groundstrokes. Every extended rally places repeated demands on the knees, and unlike a muscle injury that might respond relatively predictably to reduced activity, an overuse condition can return when the affected tissue is subjected to its previous workload. And that’s why that comment matters. Surgery is rarely necessary for ITBS, but that does not mean recovery is straightforward. According to the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons , most patients return to running within approximately six weeks of conservative treatment, although recovery depends on severity and duration. The Cleveland Clinic estimates that roughly 50% to 90% of patients improve within four to eight weeks. The Hoosiers’ game against the Golden Gophers will be under a microscope. Four of the Hoosiers’ past five games have been close in the fourth quarter with Indiana needing to make plays late in each. On top of that, ESPN’s College Gameday will be in town. Here’s what stood out from Cignetti’s availability: Josh Hoover’s health and play Josh Hoover suffered an injury to his throwing arm against Ohio State and didn’t quite look the same for the remainder of that matchup, wincing after throws. That seemed to carry over into the Michigan game when Indiana struggled mightily in the passing game. The Hoosiers pulled that one out thanks to some late plays from Hoover in overtime. item.title: Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe faces boycott in China over viral comment
item.description: Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe faces boycott in China over viral comment Kylian Mbappe appears to have built a rather unwanted digital footprint on the internet through the viral Dictator meme. Mbappe, who himself reacted to the meme in a playful manner in a recent interview, has now found himself losing sponsors as well because of the same memes. This is because multiple high-profile Chinese sponsors have pulled out after he made fun of depictions of him as Emperor Mao Zedong. Chinese companies cut ties with Mbappe As reported by Mundo Deportivo , several firms, including the Dongpeng beverage group and dairy companies Mengniu and Milkground, announced on Tuesday that they were ending their commercial cooperation with the Real Madrid star. Dongpeng, through its main account and that of its Bu Shui La brand, released official statements on Weibo confirming the immediate severing of business ties. The company cited “zero tolerance for behavior that hurts national feelings,” though it did not specify the exact reasons behind the decision. Mengniu and Milkground soon followed suit, expressing their rejection of any conduct deemed hurtful to the feelings of the Chinese people. It represents a significant commercial setback for Mbappe, whose image had been prominent across billboards, buses and elevators in Chinese cities, particularly during last summer’s World Cup. Not only that, CCTV has decided to stop broadcasting La Liga in China, taking a firm stance over Mbappe’s comments. Why the sponsors pulled out The withdrawals came in direct response to comments Mbappe, who finished second in the race for the Ballon d’Or, made when asked about his favourite meme. Mbappe walked away with nothing during the Ballon d’Or gala. (Photo by Aurelien Meunier/Getty Images) “The one I laughed at the most is the one where they use my face as a Chinese dictator. I use it a lot with my friends,” the forward said. The remark proved costly in a country where such satire is treated with the utmost seriousness. A meme superimposing Mbappe’s face onto a portrait of former leader Mao Zedong had circulated widely online, and in China, mockery of former leaders or prominent Communist Party figures can be prosecuted under laws. This is not the first time Spanish players and footballing entities have land themselves in troubled with China. Real Madrid were criticised in September over a social media post referencing Nepal and Tibet, Barcelona apologised in April after a Taiwanese flag appeared on an academy-linked page. Meanwhile, Dean Huijsen issued an apology earlier this year over content deemed offensive towards Asian citizens.

item.description: Abhishek Sharma has hit 11 centuries in T20 cricket [Getty Images] Third T20, Wellington New Zealand 198-3 (20 overs): Mitchell 89 (52); Singh 1-33 India 199-4 (13.2 overs): Abhishek 113 (38); Jamieson 2-45 India won by six wickets; lead series 3-0 Scorecard Abhishek Sharma struck a 35-ball century in India's astonishing chase of 199 in just 13.2 overs in the third T20 against New Zealand in Wellington. Abhishek and teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blitzed 133 in seven overs for the first wicket, with their powerplay score of 118 setting a new record for international T20s. Fifteen-year-old Sooryavanshi's 45 from 19 balls was merely a supporting act to Abhishek, who raced to his fifty from 15 deliveries as New Zealand's bowlers wilted. After the youngster's departure in the eighth over, Abhishek helped India cruise towards their target, falling for 113 from 38 balls - which included nine fours and 11 sixes. He fell short of equalling his record for India's fastest T20 hundred, which came off 30 balls against Afghanistan last month. India's middle order then ticked off the remaining 21 runs required with ease, with New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner's figures of 1-17 off three overs an outlier in a painful match for bowlers. item.title: Mbappé dropped by major Chinese brands as backlash grows over Mao joke
item.description: A backlash has erupted on Chinese social media over Mbappé's comments on a "Chinese dictator" [Getty Images] Several Chinese brands have dropped French footballer Kylian Mbappé following a backlash over alleged comments referring to the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Mbappé reportedly told a French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator...they put my....", he laughs, as they cut to a meme of his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao. The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward's nickname - "the dictator" - because of his huge influence in football. It has led to many such memes involving Mbappé. But the joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead. There have been a few people who have come out in support of Mbappé on Chinese social media. But theirs is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics. And few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands have been so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like Mbappé. The BBC has reached out to Mbappe and Real Madrid for comment. The Bridge is hosted by Mbappé's Real Madrid teammate Aurélien Tchouaméni. The original video is not available on the show's YouTube channel, and it's unclear when the interview first aired. In the unverified clips that have been circulating online, Mbappé does not identify Mao by name. He says he "uses [the meme] with friends all the time". The furore appeared to kick off on Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people". Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid. But some have blurred the meme itself as well as the part of the comment they found offensive, when Mbappe refers to "a Chinese dictator". Dongqiudi said in its statement that it was "unable to translate" his comments because they were "offensive to China and the Chinese people". So, many people are also wondering what exactly Mbappe said and have responded to the angry posts and comments with questions, wanting to know more.
